patches.reason: The recovered GCC 16.2 ARM cross-compile fails with a fortified snprintf format-truncation diagnostic promoted to an error. A newly reconstructed full target.c translation unit reproduces the same diagnostic and compiles with this buffer bound. Disabling partial inlining, reducing fortification to 2 or removing it does not fix the warning. Public callers exclude negative ordinals and snprintf bounds writes; no reachable overflow is established. The extracted private-helper fixture separately tests defensive full-int capacity. The actual hardened shared-runtime build still fails unpatched; this bound and a smaller unsigned-format candidate both build and pass six selected upstream C/Fortran programs each on ARM QEMU. Valid-domain private-helper checks also pass, but these are not a full DejaGNU suite or positive offload-device coverage. Keep this build repair pending human review and GCC-channel resolution.
patches.removeWhen: Remove when the original affected compiler/configuration builds libgomp without this patch. Retain exact options and newly reconstructed preprocessed source with its provenance. A GCC report or mailing-list patch requires an actual-code reproduction and applicable runtime-library validation; do not present private negative-input truncation as a valid public-API defect.
